Validation: surface pressure on the 7.1° titanium tip cone is within about 1–2.5% of the exact Taylor–Maccoll solution. Nose wave drag from the GPU solver and from OpenFOAM agrees within 0.5% at M2.0, 3.0 and 5.3. Refining the grid from 0.9 mm to 0.4 mm cells changes nose drag by less than 0.5%.

At Mach 1.5–2 the CFD-based build-up matches the generic drag curve used in this review's rough apogee check. Above Mach 3 it is roughly half of it (Cd ≈ 0.15 vs 0.32 at M5.3, before fin wave drag). The sustainer burns out near Mach 5, so the low-drag end of the apogee range is the more likely one. RASAero's ~152 km is the credible prediction, and the 150 km FAA ceiling (Finding 2.1) is an active constraint.

Above Mach 2, skin friction and base drag dominate the total. Surface finish therefore moves the apogee noticeably (the RASAero file uses 'Rough Camouflage Paint'), so the dispersion analysis needs a drag uncertainty band, not a single curve.

Not covered: fin wave drag and fin/body interference (needs 3D), power-on base drag, the stage-1 and stage-2 stacks, and viscous effects on the pressure field. A useful next step is to compare these components against RASAero's component breakdown for the same configuration. Case files, solver and scripts are in the CFD folder.
